title: Connection stacking, retry harmonization, and customer escalation play for sporadic 5xx bursts
creator: Marco Liu
description:
Summary:
Customers reported intermittent clusters of 5xx responses and timeouts during peak tenant bursts over the past 48 hours. Pattern analysis shows short windows where backend latency increases (~200-600ms) and our retry behavior + connection pooling amplifies load, causing a cascade of 5xx responses for a subset of tenants.

Observed signals:
- Spike windows correlate with tenant-burst events and long-lived client connections (streaming and non-streaming).
- Proxy logs show many concurrent in-flight requests from the same tenant reaching the runtime; when a downstream worker slows the queue depth increases and clients' SDKs trigger fast retries (no jitter) which re-fanout additional requests.
- KV cache eviction rates rose during bursts for certain request shapes (long prefix keys), contributing to higher compaction work and CPU jitter on some GPU hosts.
- Traces sampled from affected tenants show repeated identical request payloads being retried within 500ms intervals (exp-backoff missing for some SDK versions).

Hypothesis / Root cause:
A combination of: (1) client SDKs that default to aggressive immediate retries, (2) lack of a per-tenant in-flight cap at the proxy level, and (3) connection pooling behaviour that causes connection stacking (many logical requests mapped to a small set of slow connections) creates retry amplification during transient downstream latency increases. This pushes some workers to 100% CPU and triggers queuing/5xx.

Proposed mitigation (short-term):
1) Immediately deploy a proxy-side soft throttle: per-tenant in-flight request cap (default 200), with fast-fail when exceeded and a 429 guidance header linking to customer escalation docs. Canary to 5% of traffic in us-west-2.
2) Temporarily apply conservative retry harmonization rules (server-side override for SDKs without explicit jitter): gate retries to exponential backoff min 200ms with jitter and max attempts 3. Enforce at proxy for problematic tenants.
3) Adjust connection pool keepalive and max connections to avoid stacking (reduce max idle connections per upstream from 16->8 for affected pools) and add staggered connection warmups.
4) Disable non-essential KV cache compaction during burst windows (toggle via runtime feature flag) to reduce background CPU pressure.

Longer-term fixes (next milestones):
- Add per-tenant adaptive concurrency limiter integrated with historical P50/P95 latency profiles.
- SDK release: update official SDKs to include sane retry defaults and automatic jitter; publish migration guide.
- Improve tracing sampling for burst windows and add an automated detector that annotates tenant state when retry amplification is observed.
- Model-serving kernel scheduling improvements to reduce CPU jitter during cache compaction.

Acceptance criteria / Success metrics:
- Reduction of 5xx rate for affected tenants by >= 80% during similar burst profiles within the canary region.
- Decrease in retry amplification metric (retries-per-failed-request) to < 1.5.
- No regression in latency p50 for non-affected tenants (>99% of tenants see <=5% change).
- Runbook executed successfully for two simulated tenant surge scenarios in staging.

Rollout plan:
- Feb 15: Deploy proxy-side soft throttle and retry harmonization to us-west-2 canary (5%). Monitor for 2 hours.
- Feb 15: If stable, expand to 25% and run customer-impact checks.
- Feb 16: Full global rollout if metrics are green.
- Feb 18: Begin SDK rollouts and runtime feature flags for KV compaction gating.

Related artifacts and links:
- Initial customer thread (Zendesk): https://zendesk.redwood.ai/agent/tickets/11234
- Triage notes and timeline: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/ENG-47612+connection+stacking+triage
- Draft PR for proxy caps and retry override: https://github.com/redwood-inference/proxy/pull/2587
- KV compaction runtime flag PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1193

Notes for support / customer comms:
- Provide impacted customers a temporary mitigation header with guidance and ETA for permanent fix.
- If customer requires immediate SLA exception, route to escalation oncall (email: escalations@redwood.ai).
